explanation: Iterate the tree in inorder using an explicit stack, then require each value to be strictly smaller than the next. Strict comparison rejects duplicate keys.
spaceComplexity: O(n + h) auxiliary space for the materialized values and traversal stack.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: For any binary tree, the strict BST property is equivalent to strictly increasing inorder values. Inorder places all left descendants before their ancestor and all right descendants after it. Any nonincreasing adjacent pair proves an ordering violation; if every pair increases, every subtree has the required global ordering.
walkthrough: For [7,3,10,1,8], inorder values are [1,3,8,7,10]. The decrease from 8 to 7 shows that 8 lies incorrectly inside the root’s left subtree. Return false, even though 8 exceeds its immediate parent 3.
edgeCases: Duplicate keys are invalid in this strict BST contract.
Checking only direct parent-child comparisons misses ancestor violations.
